corrections.source_says: Add the separate formative interview study: six professional designers (D1-D6), interviewed remotely for 60 minutes, with qualitative analysis of workflows and challenges. It has no assigned AI-assistance contrast or scored creative-output outcome and is not an eligible experiment. The paper explicitly distinguishes this sample from the 12-person user evaluation; do not combine their participant counts.

corrections.source_says: Set any=true. Both authors are affiliated with CyberAgent; the designers were recruited from their company, participation was part of regular paid work, and the company internal ethics board approved both studies. These statements establish company involvement without implying any additional funding arrangement.
corrections.quote: The designers participated in the study as part of their regular work and were not compensated in addition to their normal pay.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 1, author affiliations; p. 5, Sec. 3.1; p. 13, Sec. 6.1

corrections.form_value: Twelve designers from the authors' company (CyberAgent) each completed four graphic-design briefs, two with Brief2Design (a structured, multi-step text-to-image design tool) and two with a ChatGPT-like conversational baseline that used the same LLM and image model. The task order was fixed and the system order was counterbalanced within each task condition (low and high design freedom). The authors computed image and prompt diversity within each participant's set of two images per task (DreamSim and text-embedding-3-large embeddings), and also measured completion, time, and Creativity Support Index ratings.
corrections.source_says: Say that the designers undertook or were assigned four tasks, rather than that each completed all four: some tasks were incomplete. Two images was the submission target, not the size of every generated-image set; diversity was calculated separately for all logged final images generated and for the two submitted images, with corresponding prompt sets.
corrections.quote: The completion rates for the low-freedom tasks were 66.7% (8/12) with the proposed system and 91.7% (11/12) with the baseline,

corrections.source_says: Record the outcome-specific exclusions/missingness here, as well as in the participant description. Diversity tests retained paired tasks with two submitted images: 7 paired participants for low-freedom tasks and 8 for high-freedom tasks. P4's low-freedom Baseline observation was excluded from completion-time analysis after submission with an experimenter's help. The overall 12-person study count does not mean all 12 contributed to every diversity comparison.
corrections.quote: For this analysis, we use the paired data of the tasks where participants submitted two images, resulting in 7 data points for the low-freedom tasks and 8 for the high-freedom tasks.

corrections.source_says: Use flexibility for prompt diversity, consistently with the image-diversity outcomes: the score describes variety within each participant's own task-specific set of prompts. It is not diversity across different people, so question="with_ai" remains appropriate.
corrections.quote: We computed the image and prompt diversity scores for the sets of images and prompts generated and submitted by participants.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 15, Sec. 6.5; p. 18, Sec. 7.3; creativity-codebook.md, Sec. 6 (within-person variety is flexibility)

corrections.form_value: ["Image diversity of submitted images (average pairwise 1 - cosine of DreamSim embeddings within a participant's set for one task)", "Image diversity of all generated images (average pairwise 1 - cosine of DreamSim embeddings within a participant's set for one task)", "Prompt diversity (average pairwise 1 - cosine of OpenAI text-embedding-3-large embeddings of the prompts within a participant's set for one task)"]
corrections.source_says: Add the participant-level number of generated final images as a fluency outcome (with_ai; system-log category count). Brief2Design vs Baseline: low-freedom M=4.2 (SD=1.4) vs 4.8 (SD=2.1), t(11)=-1.07, p=.309; high-freedom M=3.8 (SD=0.9) vs 5.4 (SD=1.2), t(11)=-4.71, p=.001. This analysis covers the 12-person sample, unlike the restricted diversity analyses. Element-level preview images were not logged.
corrections.quote: in the high-freedom tasks, they generated 3.8 (𝑆𝐷= 0.9) and 5.4 (𝑆𝐷= 1.2), respectively.

corrections.source_says: For the existing outcomes, populate treatment_arm="Brief2Design", control_arm="Baseline", comparison_type="ai_design", and statistics_available=["test_statistic"]. Image-diversity results show no clear difference. Prompt diversity is significantly higher for generated low-freedom and submitted high-freedom sets, with no clear difference for the other two tests; record these condition-specific directions rather than leave direction empty. These are two AI configurations using the same models, not an AI-versus-no-AI comparison.
corrections.quote: We used the same image generation model and LLM as in our proposed system.

corrections.source_says: Set ai_available_when_produced="yes" and timing="immediate" for the existing outcomes. The scored images and corresponding prompts were generated during the tool-assisted tasks; these are not post-removal or delayed outcomes.
corrections.quote: The system logs include the time of each image generation and submission, the generated images and their corresponding prompts, the submitted images, and the task completion status.

corrections.source_says: Use "not_stated" for preregistered and for each outcome's primary status. No preregistration or primary-outcome designation is stated in the full document, including its appendices; empty strings are not offered values for these fields.
corrections.quote: The experiment aimed to assess how effectively Brief2Design operationalizes the design goals relative to the baseline interaction style.
corrections.locator: PDF pp. 13-19, Secs. 6-7; full-document check including pp. 26-34; form-spec.md, Rule 1 and JSON structure

corrections.form_value: Within-subjects experiment with 12 designers (p. 13, Sec. 6.1), well below 50; the diversity tests use only 7 and 8 participants per task condition (p. 18, Sec. 7.3). Both arms use generative AI (an ai_design contrast), and the system order was counterbalanced, with no statement that it was randomized (p. 14, Sec. 6.3). The diversity scores are computed within each participant's own set of images, so they measure within-person variety, not diversity across people. Listed in the screening report as a randomized-style experiment below 50 participants.
corrections.source_says: Replace "a randomized-style experiment" with "a counterbalanced within-subject experiment with randomization not stated". Counterbalancing does not document random allocation to system orders. Retain criterion_1="unclear", null randomized counts, core="no", and the below-50 exclusion; the full text does not establish a randomized people study.
corrections.quote: The order of the four tasks was fixed, while the order of the systems was counterbalanced within each task condition.

corrections.form_value: Among 12 company designers, Brief2Design did not change the image diversity of submitted designs relative to a conversational baseline (low-freedom t(6) = 1.91, p = .105; high-freedom t(7) = .820, p = .439) but raised prompt diversity (e.g., submitted high-freedom t(7) = 2.45, p = .044) (p. 18, Sec. 7.3; p. 17, Figs. 8-9).
corrections.source_says: Replace "did not change" with "showed no statistically significant difference"; the tests do not establish equivalence or no effect. Qualify the prompt result: significant increases were reported for generated low-freedom prompts (t(6)=3.86, p=.008) and submitted high-freedom prompts (t(7)=2.45, p=.044), but not the other two comparisons. The three statistics already quoted in the one-line finding match the PDF; the relevant paired samples contain 7 and 8 participants, not all 12.
corrections.quote: The t-test revealed no significant differences in image diversity across systems

confirmed: Read the complete markdown conversion through Appendix B and checked the relevant PDF pages. The file has 34 pages and its first-page stamp is arXiv:2604.11019v1 [cs.HC], 13 Apr 2026; the recorded title, authors, and source.version are correct (PDF p. 1 and document page count).

The evaluation is a remote within-subject comparison of two generative-AI configurations with fixed task order and counterbalanced system order; randomization is not stated (PDF pp. 13-15, Secs. 6.2-6.4). Retaining design_class="other", assignment.randomized="not_stated", and context_class="none" is appropriate pending allocation information; neither an RCT classification nor a definitive nonrandom-allocation claim is established.

The user-evaluation sample is 12 professional designers, all using both systems, not 12 independent people per arm. Reported demographics match: 7 women, 5 men, mean age 27.1, design experience 5 months to 20 years, mean 4.2 years (PDF p. 13, Secs. 6.1 and 6.3). Randomized counts remain null.

The diversity tests use 7 paired participant observations for low-freedom tasks and 8 for high-freedom tasks, restricted to paired tasks with two submitted images; these are not counts of texts, images, or ratings (PDF p. 18, Sec. 7.3). The overall study and every reported outcome-specific sample are below 50 people.

Both systems use GPT-4o and gpt-image-1 (PDF p. 13, Secs. 5.5-6.2; p. 26, Appendix A). Each designer was assigned four briefs, two under each freedom condition, with two images requested per task; the task limit was 15 minutes and the total procedure approximately 120 minutes including practice (PDF pp. 13-15, Secs. 6.3-6.4). The four task descriptions match Appendix B (PDF pp. 30-34).

Diversity is the mean pairwise dissimilarity, 1 minus cosine similarity, within a participant-task set; image embeddings use DreamSim and prompt embeddings use text-embedding-3-large (PDF p. 15, Sec. 6.5; p. 18, Sec. 7.3). Image outcomes therefore fit flexibility/with_ai, not across_people. Unlogged element-level preview images are excluded (PDF p. 15, Sec. 6.5).

S1-O1 reported statistics match exactly: submitted-image diversity, low freedom t(6)=1.91, p=.105; high freedom t(7)=.820, p=.439 (PDF p. 18, Sec. 7.3). Figure 8 marks both comparisons ns and shows means graphically without numerical mean labels (PDF p. 17).

S1-O2 reported statistics match exactly: generated-image diversity, low freedom t(6)=.824, p=.441; high freedom t(7)=-1.16, p=.283 (PDF p. 18, Sec. 7.3). Figure 8 marks both comparisons ns and shows means graphically without numerical mean labels (PDF p. 17).

S1-O3 reported statistics match exactly: generated-prompt diversity, low freedom t(6)=3.86, p=.008 and high freedom t(7)=1.69, p=.134; submitted-prompt diversity, low freedom t(6)=2.00, p=.093 and high freedom t(7)=2.45, p=.044 (PDF p. 18, Sec. 7.3). Brief2Design mean markers are higher in all four Figure 9 comparisons, but only two tests are significant at .05 (PDF p. 17).

Core exclusion is correct because fewer than 50 people were analyzed, while the image/prompt distances are scored on task outputs (PDF p. 13, Sec. 6.1; p. 15, Sec. 6.5; p. 18, Sec. 7.3). The CSI and feature-usefulness surveys are self-reports, not scored creative-output outcomes (PDF p. 15, Sec. 6.4; pp. 18-19, Sec. 7.4).

This is an original formative study plus user evaluation, not a synthesis or an AI-versus-human-output benchmark; synthesis defaults are appropriate and there are no pooled estimates to verify (PDF p. 5, Sec. 3; pp. 13-19, Secs. 6-7; p. 23, Sec. 9).
summary: This is a 12-designer counterbalanced study with unreported randomization; its diversity statistics match the PDF and use 7 or 8 paired participants. Corrections address an omitted study and outcome, appendices, company involvement, incomplete coding, and overstated findings.
